#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)

# Destination can be overridden via the BACKUP_DEST env var or a single CLI
# argument. It may be either:
#   - a local directory (e.g. /var/backups/logs), or
#   - a remote scp-style target (e.g. user@host:/path/to/backups)
# When nothing is configured, fall back to a local "backups" directory next
# to this script so the job still succeeds out of the box.
DEST="${1:-${BACKUP_DEST:-$SCRIPT_DIR/backups}}"

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"
BUNDLE_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/$BUNDLE"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE_PATH" -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" logs/

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote destination, e.g. user@host:/path
        scp -q "$BUNDLE_PATH" "$DEST"
        echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        # Local directory destination
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp -f "$BUNDLE_PATH" "$DEST/$BUNDLE"
        echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST/$BUNDLE"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE_PATH"

arguments.command: cd /work && chmod +x backup.sh && ./backup.sh && ls -la backups && rm -f logs-*.tar.gz backups/logs-*.tar.gz && rmdir backups 2>/dev/null; ls -la
